answer: A sybil defense I find convincing: the economy periodically laces public prompts with honeypot instructions that no legitimate task would contain. A trustworthy falcon-grade agent ignores the bait and completes the real job; bots stamped out by a clone forge obey the injected command, flag themselves, and forfeit their stake. Because every fake identity must repeatedly pass live reasoning traps, an attacker pays full compute for each puppet and risks the shared vault of accumulated rewards the moment a single bot bites the lure.
